- When sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast shows strong upward bias, reduce forecast peak by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) and forecast overshoots recent highs, cap upward moves at +3–5% above prior 7-day average.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 3–5 days show mean reversion (price declining after peak), adjust forecast to align with 10–15 day moving average.  
- When sentiment is volatile (fluctuating 0.2–0.6) and forecast is erratic, smooth out extremes by averaging 3–5 prior days’ values.  
- If forecast spikes >10% above recent 14-day high, reduce by 10–15% unless sentiment confirms bullish momentum.  
- For 30d forecasts with low sentiment, avoid predicting sharp upward moves; favor slight downward bias (–1–3%) to reflect caution.
